Let me analyze. The mitosis scene: metaphase bipolar attachment then anaphase separation. Measured anchors coincide at end. Chromatid shapes: sister_A points [[-0.45,-0.85],[-0.12,0],[-0.45,0.85]] — a ">" chevron pointing right (toward center). sister_B points [[0.45,-0.85],[0.12,0],[0.45,0.85]] — "<" pointing left. So the V apex points inward toward each other, kinetochores at center (-0.285) which is on the outer... wait, kinetochore_A center -0.285 is the average; the apex at -0.12 is rightward. Hmm, during anaphase, chromatids move poleward with kinetochore leading; typical V shape arms trail behind. Here sister_A moves left toward left pole, apex points right (trailing? apex is at -0.12, right of center -0.285). Arms at -0.45 (left, toward pole). So arms lead toward pole and kinetochore region trails — inverted V orientation. Actually kinetochore at center -0.285, apex -0.12 to the right. The shape looks like ">" with the point facing away from direction of motion. In real anaphase, kinetochore leads poleward and arms trail toward the equator, giving V with apex toward pole. Here arms (at x=-0.45) are closer to left pole than the apex; so arms lead. That's a minor schematic geometry issue — could be flagged as minor/uncertain. But is it a blocker? It's a schematic chevron; the kinetochore bead sits at center, arms extend poleward. Arguably minor teaching detail, not observed scientific error requiring revise. Hmm.

Also caption truncation: captions run off screen edges ("er kinetochores attach..." and "...metaphase p"). That's a layout/readability issue — text clipped, but scientific meaning still conveyed? The instruction says layout change alone cannot fix mechanism; but readability issue is minor. Caption overflow is an assembly/animation issue, minor.

Also labels overlap during motion ("Daughter B" overlapping ghost text) — minor.

Key checks: attachment precedes separation (preconditions enforced), identity continuity, two chromatids no cloning, measured coincidence 0.0, direction of motion verified over full trajectory (centers -0.285 → -2.8 and +0.285 → +2.8, monotonic). Microtubules shorten (end follows kinetochore). Good.

One concern: microtubule end during motion lags? At t=9.67, sister_A center -0.844, microtubule end -1.583 — that's ahead of kinetochore (overshoot toward pole). At t=11.13, center -2.073, mt end -2.735 — again ahead. So during transit the microtubule end is not coincident with kinetochore; gap ~0.74 and 0.66. Actually the mt end is beyond the kinetochore toward the pole, meaning microtubule passes through/past the chromatid... In frames 10.2s and 11.2s, the line ends before reaching the chromatid? Frame 10.2: line from pole ends at x≈345px, chromatid at ~410px. So the microtubule end is short of the chromatid — detached during motion! Wait pixel mapping: pole at x=212 corresponds to -4; center 480 = 0. So scale ~67 px/unit. mt end -1.583 → 480-106=374 px; observed line ends ~345. Chromatid A center -0.844 → 424 px; frame shows chromatid at ~410. Hmm mt end at 374 vs kinetochore 424: line ends left of kinetochore, i.e., gap between microtubule tip and kinetochore ~50px = 0.74 units. So during anaphase transit the microtubule appears detached from the kinetochore (gap), reconnecting at the end. That is a real observed connection error: attachment not maintained during poleward movement — visible gap. The declared relation bipolar_attachment persists but drawn link endpoint lags behind (interpolation mismatch, likely mt uses different easing/time base). This is a major issue: kinetochore–microtubule attachment must remain continuous during anaphase A movement.

Indeed frames 10.2 and 11.2 show clear gaps between line tip and white bead. That's an observed scientific/mechanistic error (spindle attachment lost mid-anaphase). Constraint only checked after metaphase (and final coincidence at 13s passes because motion ends). So issue: major, root_cause ANIMATION_IMPLEMENTATION, target microtubule_left/right, kinetochore_A/B, event anaphase (transition anaphase_chromatid_separation_1). Acceptance: max distance ≤0.04 at all sampled times during anaphase.

Second issue: chevron orientation — arms lead poleward, apex/kinetochore trailing; minor/uncertain. I'd flag minor with uncertainty since schematic. Actually kinetochore bead is at center, and shape apex points equatorward — arms toward pole. Real anaphase chromosomes: kinetochore leading, arms trailing equatorward. So arms poleward is inverted. Minor.

Third: caption clipping off both edges — minor readability, blocks verifying full text. Could combine as minor. Max 3 issues. Decision REVISE.
